SECRET

P.F. 41426/B.4a.

The Chief Constable,
Special Branch.

On the 12th April, 1939, under your reference 335/MP/2014, you sent me a letter regarding Hamilton N. S. Gould VERSCHOYLE. This man is undoubtedly Hamilton Neil Stuart GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE who was known to me about ten years ago as a prominent member of the Society for Cultural Relations with the U.S.S.R. He was born in Dublin on 19.12.1904 and was granted passport No. 13365 on the 26th March, 1924. This was subsequently renewed up to the 26th March, 1933. VERSCHOYLE left for Russia on the 2nd October, 1930, and arrived back from Leningrad, travelling on a Free State passport, on or about the 11th August, 1932.

In October, 1933, the High Commissioner of the Irish Free State forwarded to the Passport Office the names of a number of people from whom it was recommended that passport facilities should be withheld, in view of their close association with Communist and allied organisations. Amongst these names was included Niall de GOLD VERSHOYLE and we have taken this to refer to Hamilton Neil Stuart GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE. As, however, it appears from the copies of letters which you have sent me that the Dublin Police know nothing of VERSCHOYLE, it would appear that we are wrong in this assumption.

18th April, 1939.
